The Shenzhen summit may give Vladimir Putin a big stage, and a bright spotlight.

It does not necessarily bring him closer to winning the war.
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Correspondent's assessment that diplomatic gains do not translate into military victory.

quote_text:
Last month Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the Putin-Trump-Xi meeting might resemble the Yalta Conference of 1945. That is when the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States – Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt - met to re-organise post-World War Two Europe.

"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," said Zelensky.
speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Ukraine's fear of a great-power carve-up of spheres of influence.

quote_text: And the Ukrainian strike on the road bridge linking Russia to the Crimean Peninsula – carried out on the eve of the summit - was a blow to Moscow's prestige. The attack severely damaged part of the multi-billion-dollar bridge built by Russia after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine.
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Major Ukrainian strike severely damaging the Crimean bridge, a key logistics link.

quote_text: It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Notes continued Russian strikes and Kremlin rejection of an unconditional ceasefire.

quote_text:
Among European leaders, and especially in Ukraine, there is concern that the three-way meeting might produce more than just a pretty picture, though not in a good way for Kyiv.

Donald Trump has already said that in Shenzhen he wants to discuss his "favourite subject" - the war in Ukraine. The Kremlin would likely welcome an opportunity to argue its case to Trump and Xi without Ukrainian officials or European leaders in the room.
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Highlights risk of Ukraine's fate being discussed without Kyiv or Europe present.

quote_text: "We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced unprecedented sanctions pressure," Putin told a business forum of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation organisation.
speaker: Vladimir Putin
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Putin claims Western sanctions and isolation have failed.

quote_text:
Nearly five years after President Putin launched his so-called "special military operation", Russia is still struggling to win its war on Ukraine.

Over this time, it has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.
article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
rationale: Assessment that Russia has not achieved military victory despite heavy losses.

quote_text: Russian forces, like Ukraine's, have built fortified positions inside the pipeline. They still try to infiltrate Ukrainian positions, burrowing their way in and out of the pipe.
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Shows the underground battle remains contested by Russia.

quote_text:
It has taken Ukraine seven months to clear 15km of the pipeline.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed it as a success.

It has helped retake lost territory and been a boost for morale, but on its own it has not changed the course of the war.
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Assesses the operation's limited strategic impact despite tactical gains.

quote_text:
But, Zanuda believes it is the best way to fight in the future. "Ground operations are now nearly impossible," he said, adding that "everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground".

There'll be more missions like this, he believes. "Pipelines run everywhere," he said. "You have to remember, back in the Soviet times, oil, gas and ammonia were being transported to Europe, with the entire transit route running through Ukraine."
speaker: Zanuda, Ukrainian tunnel operation planner
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Expectation that underground warfare will expand as surface operations become near impossible.

quote_text: Over the course of the operation Ukraine says it killed more than 100 Russian soldiers and took 30 prisoners.
speaker: Ukraine
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Gives claimed casualty and prisoner figures for the operation.

quote_text: Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) along the pipeline.
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Quantifies Ukraine's progress in the underground operation near Kupyansk.

quote_text:
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.

With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Shows drone saturation has made surface advances nearly impossible, driving new underground tactics.

quote_text: The Russians were the first to exploit the pipe to infiltrate the nearby city of Kupyansk in September 2025. They have used underground pipelines before, during the capture of the city of Avdiivka in 2024, and last year in their bid to recapture areas of Russia's Kursk region.
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Documents Russia's repeated use of pipeline infiltration tactics in key battles.

quote_text:
Hundreds of Colombian volunteers have also been involved in the operation, part of the RUG 23rd Assault Regiment.

Foreign fighters have helped boost Ukraine's depleted ranks.
article_title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
rationale: Points to Ukraine's manpower shortages and reliance on foreign fighters.
